Pedagogy

/PED-uh-goh-jee/ - the stress falls on PED · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pedagogy means the theory and practice of teaching.

Two tutors, one pedagogy: never hand over the answer, always hand over the next question.

Worked Example

The mountain guides' school ran three generations on inherited pedagogy — knots first, then weather, then rock — until a new director arrived with accident data arguing weather should come first. The quarrel that followed wasn't about climbing; it was about pedagogy: what gets taught in what order, and why.

Pedagogy is teaching's own discipline — not any single lesson, but the field itself. A school can overhaul its pedagogy without changing a single book on the reading list: same material, taught on new principles. Pedagogical is this word's adjective; didactic describes work bent on instructing you.

How Pedagogy Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

teaching craft

teaching craft: the how of teaching, named plainly

instruction

instruction: the delivering of lessons, without the theory behind it

Antonyms

winging it

winging it: improvised teaching with no method behind it

rote drill

rote drill: mechanical repetition, deaf to how learning works

How Strong Is It? — schooling → instruction → pedagogy

schooling vs. pedagogy

schooling vs. pedagogy: Schooling is the plainest rung — the receiving of lessons, with nothing said about how they are designed.

instruction vs. pedagogy

instruction vs. pedagogy: Instruction stops short of pedagogy: it is the delivering of lessons, while pedagogy studies how those lessons should be built and why they work.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of pedagogy.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ped-

Root — ped-: child (Greek pais, paid-)

Root — agog-

Root — agog-: leader, guiding (Greek agogos)

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: noun: the practice of

Put it together

Put it together: Ped- (child) + agog- (leader) + -y = the practice of leading children. In Athens the paidagogos only walked the child to school; the centuries promoted him. Today pedagogy is the whole science of the walk — how anyone is led from not knowing to knowing. (This ped- is Greek for child; the pedal-and-pedestrian ped- is Latin for foot.)

Use the root in a new word: pediatrician

Use the root in a new word: pediatrician: The pediatrician marks each visit on the same growth chart, birth to twelfth grade.

Word Choice

academic

Pedagogy is the discipline's name for itself — say it when discussing teaching as a field of theory and research. For the adjective, pedagogical; for a tone that pushes its lesson, didactic. In casual talk, 'teaching methods' does the same honest work.
